velocity.title: Daily outflow within $25,000?
velocity.intent: Monitoring should identify activity that needs review. The entry conditions determine which movements reach this detector.
velocity.behavior: The API first totals today’s qualifying outgoing movements across four rails. If the total including this movement exceeds $25,000, it blocks and returns before the large-movement detector.
velocity.boundary: This ordering means a velocity-blocked movement does not reach this detector. The book-transfer handler also has a safe-mode gate before runGate. This trace starts inside runGate; it does not cover every earlier refusal or replay.
velocity.contract: Reads transfer, wire_transfer, ach_transfer and card_authorization. Uses UTC day boundaries and selected statuses; it is not a rolling 24-hour window.

threshold.title: Movement greater than $10,000?
threshold.intent: BSA-06 calls for monitoring to generate alerts for review. This amount rule is one implementation choice, not the full policy.
threshold.behavior: A movement greater than $10,000 creates a passing control result and calls the alert writer. Exactly $10,000 does not match this rule.
threshold.boundary: The alert is named ctr_threshold in code. That name alone does not demonstrate that cash reporting obligations are satisfied.
threshold.contract: Writes control_result with decision=pass. subject_ref is the source account; entity_hash is SHA-256 of the source account ID.

blocked.title: Block the movement
blocked.intent: The policy-to-implementation review needs to account for paths that end before alert generation.
blocked.behavior: Records a blocking velocity result, updates the movement to its rail-specific rejection status, and returns an error.
blocked.boundary: This is a neighboring payment gate, included here because it changes this control’s reach.
blocked.contract: Returns blocked=true and velocity_limit_exceeded. Writes are awaited and errors throw.

alert.title: Open an alert for review
alert.intent: Each alert should be triaged within two business days of creation.
alert.behavior: Writes the causing event, an open alert with its triage deadline, then a timer event. The same movement and alert type produce a stable alert ID.
alert.boundary: The calendar skips weekends, but not federal holidays. Creating an alert does not itself stop the payment; later payment gates still apply.
alert.contract: Ordered upserts: bsa_alert.created → bsa_alert → bsa_alert.triage.timer. Duplicate IDs are ignored. Any write error throws; these are separate writes.

skip.title: No alert from this rule
skip.intent: The overall monitoring obligation may be served by several detectors with different scopes.
skip.behavior: Amounts at or below $10,000 skip this detector. Subsequent structuring and other payment checks can still run.
skip.boundary: “No alert from this rule” does not mean the movement is safe, compliant, or guaranteed to settle.
skip.contract: Control returns to the remainder of runGate. This branch is not the end of payment processing.

access.title: An investigator opens the alert
access.intent: BSA-06 assigns opening and closing cases to the Investigations role.
access.behavior: Partner requests receive 404. Internal actors without the required role receive 403. An already-triaged alert replays the original result.
access.boundary: The diagram shows authorization at this endpoint. It does not establish the integrity of every credential or identity source.
access.contract: POST /bsa/alerts/{id}/triage. Loads the alert by ID; a missing alert returns 404. Previously triaged rows are not re-decided.

triage.title: Does this alert need investigation?
triage.intent: Alerts should be triaged within two business days. Alerts unresolved at triage should escalate to a case.
triage.behavior: The API accepts an investigator’s resolved or escalated outcome. Resolving requires a nonempty explanation; escalation opens an investigation.
triage.boundary: This endpoint records a human judgment. It does not determine whether the explanation is substantively adequate or automatically escalate when time expires.
triage.contract: Validates outcome before writes. A resolved outcome without note returns a validation error.

resolve.title: Close with an explanation
resolve.intent: The review should leave enough evidence to understand why an alert did not become a case.
resolve.behavior: Marks the alert triaged and closed. Attempts to emit a triage event containing the note and outcome.
resolve.boundary: The note is carried by the event, not the alert update. If event emission fails, the handler logs it and still returns success after the alert update.
resolve.contract: Alert patch stores triaged_at, triage_outcome and status. emitBsaEvent is inside a catch-and-log block.

case.title: Open an investigation
case.sub: Decision due 30 or 60 days from detection
case.intent: Unresolved alerts should become cases. Reach a SAR or no-SAR decision within 30 days of initial detection, or 60 if no suspect is identified.
case.behavior: Creates a case linked to the alert and carries alert details as evidence. Uses 60 days when the request says no suspect; otherwise 30. The clock starts at alert creation.
case.boundary: The no-suspect flag comes from the caller. Event emission failures are logged; the case insert and alert update are separate writes.
case.contract: Records opened_by=ctx.tokenId. Writes case.sar.decision.timer and case.opened events, then associates the case with the alert.

officer.title: BSA Officer authorization
officer.sub: Required role; compare the case opener’s token
officer.intent: BSA-06 gives the BSA Officer write access to SAR decisions. The implementation also checks separation from the case opener.
officer.behavior: Requires the BSA Officer role. If opened_by is populated and matches the deciding token, refuses the decision even if the token has both roles. A missing opener is not refused by this comparison.
officer.boundary: The handler compares token IDs. Confirm how credentials map to people before treating this as proof that two different people acted.
officer.contract: Same opener token returns HTTP 409 segregation_of_duties. A decided case replays its result; another closed case is rejected.

decision.title: File a SAR or do not file?
decision.sub: A written rationale is required either way
decision.intent: The policy calls for a documented SAR/no-SAR decision and committee review, with filings reported to the Board.
decision.behavior: Accepts the officer’s decision and rationale, closes the case, and records the deciding actor and any supplied concurrence list.
decision.boundary: Committee concurrence is recorded, but quorum and composition are not enforced in this handler. Board reporting is not established by this traced path.
decision.contract: concurred_by defaults to an empty list. Lateness is computed from sar_decision_due_at and included in the response and decision-event payload.

file.title: Record “file”
file.sub: Close case; start SAR retention workflow
file.intent: A filing decision should connect to filing, supporting records and the policy’s reporting duties.
file.behavior: The handler attempts to emit investigation-complete and sar.filed events, then starts the SAR retention workflow.
file.boundary: The event name is not proof of external SAR submission. This function records a decision; external filing is outside this trace. Event or retention failures are logged without failing the saved decision.
file.contract: Case update precedes events. The file branch calls startRetentionFor(db, "sar", caseId, …).

nofile.title: Record “do not file”
nofile.intent: Do-not-file decisions must be documented and retained.
nofile.behavior: Stores the rationale on the case and attempts to emit investigation-complete and no-file decision events.
nofile.boundary: This branch does not call the SAR-specific retention helper. That alone does not establish whether other retention rules cover the case.
nofile.contract: decision_rationale is saved with the closed case before event emission. Event failures are caught and logged.

decide.title: SAR decision & record
decide.output: A recorded SAR or no-SAR decision
